'''Michel Che''' (29 December 1941 – 7 August 2019) was a French chemist who completed his doctorate ([[Electron paramagnetic resonance|EPR]] study of [[titanium dioxide]]) in 1968 at the [[University of Lyon]] and studied as a postdoctoral fellow at [[Princeton University]] (1969–71). He was appointed professor at [[University of Paris VI: Pierre et Marie Curie]] in 1975 and Senior Member of the Institut Universitaire de France in 1995.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ae-info.org/ae/User/Che_Michel/CV |title=Academy of Europe: CV |publisher=[[Academia Europæa|Academy of Europe]] |accessdate=September 25, 2011}}</ref>

Che was born in [[Lyon]], France. His work has led to around 400 publications in international journals. He was very active in the promotion and organisation of [[catalysis]], being the President-Founder of [http://www.efcats.org/ EFCATS] (European Federation of Catalysis Societies) with creation in 1993 of the cycle of the now famous biennial "EuropaCat" congresses, and President of IACS (International Association of Catalysis Societies) in 2000–04,<ref>[http://www.iacs-icc.org/ "IACS"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090121072114/http://www.iacs-icc.org/ |date=2009-01-21 }}, www.iacs-icc.org.</ref> culminating with the organisation and opening of the ''13th International Congress on Catalysis'' in Paris in 2004.

His research activity has been largely devoted to catalysis processes involving gas–solid, liquid–solid and solid–solid [[interface (chemistry)|interfaces]]. He has pioneered a molecular approach to [[heterogeneous catalysis]], based on [[transition element]]s taken as probes, specific [[isotope]]s and physical techniques, which provided him with an original position in the field. His work has led to the emergence of interfacial coordination chemistry at the junction of [[colloid]]al, electro-, supramolecular, geo- and solid-state chemistries. His studies have largely contributed to improve understanding of the elementary processes involved in laboratory/industrial catalysis, and particularly water-mediated assemblies in catalyst preparation.{{Citation needed|date=September 2011}}

Michel Che's awards include: J.&nbsp;H. Van't Hoff (Netherlands), [http://www.jsps.go.jp/english/ Japan Society for the Promotion of Science] (Japan), M.&nbsp;Sklodowska-Curie and P.&nbsp;Curie (Poland), A.&nbsp;Joannides and P.&nbsp;Sue (France), Von&nbsp;Humboldt – Gay-Lussac (Germany). He is Doctor ''[[honoris causa]]'' of several universities ([http://webarchive.loc.gov/all/20050422230514/http://www.uj.edu.pl/dispatch.jsp?item=uniwersytet/wyroznienia/honoris.jsp&lang=en Cracow, Poland];  [http://arquivo.pt/wayback/20070607043418/http%3A//www.utl.pt/page.aspx?idCat%3D19 Lisbon, Portugal]; Bucharest, Romania) and member of several high-ranking academies (e.g. [[Academia Europaea]], [http://www.leopoldina-halle.de/e_index.htm Deutsche Akademie der Naturforscher Leopoldina]).

In 2014, he was awarded the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]]'s [[Faraday Lectureship Prize]].<ref name="RSCFLP">{{cite web|url=http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/FaradayLectureshipPrize/2014-Winner.asp|title=Faraday Lectureship Prize 2014 Winner|publisher=[[Royal Society of Chemistry]]|accessdate=8 October 2014}}</ref>

Che died on 7 August 2019 after a short illness.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Acad_Main/News/Michel%20Che%20%281941%20-%202019%29|title=Academy of Europe: Michel Che (1941 - 2019)|last=|first=|date=13 August 2019|website=Academy of Europe|access-date=}}</ref>
